mode: Read-only mathematical review, without independent execution of the censuses
findings: For each coordinate permutation, the XOR difference count equals the translated intersection size because each intersection vertex determines one pair.
Reversing a parent pair replaces the isometry by its inverse and preserves intersection size.
Independent canonicalization of two parents is valid for the full isometry family. It generally fails for an involution-only family.
Disjoint components obtained using an arbitrary isometry do not automatically give a global involution quotient.

For truncations, every original collision must be removed at one of its two parent vertices. A collision count at most the total deletions is necessary, with endpoint restrictions for contiguous paths.
No upper bound for all Q7 parent paths or global Q9 result follows from the saved-pair exclusions.
